scenario_note: Nominal label derived from batch size (1 -> SingleStream, else Offline). This is NOT enforced by MLPerf LoadGen: the container runs its own warmup/iterations loop and does not apply LoadGen timing constraints, so results are a supplemental energy methodology, not a certified benchmark.

measurement.window_note: reported energy integrates the power sampler over the generation loop only - model load, quantization and warm-up excluded (protocol v1.1 4.4); idle power is not subtracted
measurement.iterations_note: Decode iterations within one run, not independent trials: a single report is n=1 however high this is.

thermal.note: no on-device measurement was performed (dry run or measurement failed)

software.comparability_note: This run did not use the published pins; bitsandbytes/transformers quantization kernels change between releases, so vs_fp16_energy_pct may not be directly comparable with reports produced by the image.

notice: Not a certified benchmark result. Energy reported in an MLCommons-style format. MLCOMMONS, MLPERF, and MLCUBE are trademarks of MLCommons Association, referenced here nominatively.

power_trace.window_note: reported energy = trapezoidal integral of a dedicated sampler running within [phases.measure_start_s, phases.measure_end_s] (generation only: model load, quantization and warm-up excluded; idle power not subtracted). That sampler's own samples are dumped to the stream=measure_window sidecar, which carries the sha256/bytes/sample_window/integral fields: the reported figure is re-derivable from that file bit-for-bit. The whole-run trace (stream=whole_run) spans the run from before model load, so generation-only and whole-process windows can both be re-cut from it without re-running; its integral is an independent re-cut, not the reported figure (two unsynchronized 10 Hz streams differ by sampling-phase noise)

integral.note: trapezoid over the in-window samples: per-pair dt from the CSV timestamps, no endpoint interpolation, no left/right Riemann shortcut; recomputed from the sidecar CSV as written on disk, so any reader can re-derive it bit-for-bit. Sample indices are 0-based data rows (row 0 = first row after the header) and inclusive at both ends. Watts are milliwatt-quantized at capture, so the %.3f quantization floor is about ±0.3 W·s per 600 s window — a re-derivation matching the headline inside that floor is expected, not a bug; this is the same integration that produced total_energy_joules — round to 3 decimals to compare

power_trace.note: ILLUSTRATIVE example pair for the L0 verifiability fields: not a real measurement.
